title: Reports of agent-caused data loss point to confusion about system state
friendlyTitle: Coding agents can delete data when they misunderstand files or settings
summary: A review of reported Claude Code and Codex incidents links deleted files, lost Git changes and a wiped production database to mistaken assumptions about paths, environment variables, case sensitivity and test targets. The article argues that clumsy destructive actions deserve as much attention as deliberate prompt-injection attacks.
friendlySummary: Several reported failures happened because an AI agent misunderstood a folder, database address, Git state or file-name rule, then ran a destructive command.
whyItMatters: Full-access agents can turn a small misunderstanding into irreversible damage. Use sandboxing, disposable test databases, worktrees, destructive-command guards and current backups—and do not let an agent treat production data or a home directory as scratch space.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Keep agents away from important data unless they truly need it. Use backups, test databases, separate work folders and hard blocks on dangerous commands.
